request.notes: `task_type` is one of task/epic/gate and is ALWAYS sent even when it equals the upstream default, the same discipline the read side applies to `with_claims`; an unknown one is `invalid_task_type`, a code of its own. A `gate` requires `metadata.gate_type` in human/timer/ci/pr/external_task, and a `timer` gate additionally a parseable `metadata.ready_at` — both `invalid_input`. `metadata` must NOT carry `depends_on`/`blocked_on`: that is `invalid_metadata_key`, again its own code, because dependencies are first-class edges now. There is NO title rule — an empty title is accepted and stored, so Lens's own form validation is the only thing that refuses one (T3 D10). `depends_on` creates a `blocks` edge from each predecessor and `parent_task_id` a `parent_child` edge parent -> new task; both must already exist, and a repeated predecessor is deduplicated before insertion while the response still echoes the resolved request list. Lens writes the project under BOTH conventions (metadata.project and the project tag, §5B.1) and carries `metadata.lens_request_id` for its own best-effort de-duplication: create mints a new id and inserts with NO uniqueness on any metadata key, so the key is a Lens-side lookup, never an upstream idempotency guarantee (T3 D10). Every id goes through the SHARED resolver, whose whole domain is probed: a full id (>= 36 characters, a UUID) is handed straight to this tool's own lookup; anything shorter than SIX characters that is not an exact id is `invalid_input`; a 6-to-35-character value is searched as a PREFIX, and matching nothing is the resolver's own `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …", a different message from this tool's own not-found, same code) while matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` with up to FIVE `{id, title}` candidate RECORDS — the message states the capped count. Lens DOES send prefixes here — the create form takes a full or short id for a predecessor or parent (T3 D10) — so every one of these refusals is on a Lens request.

observed_divergences: **The success payload carries no `success` key.** Its documented return is "Dict with task_id, title, updated_at, and the resolved depends_on / parent_task_id when supplied" — the minted id IS the success signal, so `TaskCreateResult.success` is derived from it rather than read from a flag that is never sent. `depends_on` / `parent_task_id` come back as the RESOLVED full ids and are absent when the request supplied none (`no_links`). Every error envelope above IS probed live, including the two codes of its own — `invalid_task_type` and `invalid_metadata_key`, which the first passes of this slice both recorded as `invalid_input` — because each of these arguments is refused by validation BEFORE anything is inserted, so the probe creates nothing (it also cancelled anything it might have created, and created nothing). What is NOT probed is the success payload and the empty-title behaviour: both would insert a task into the operator's store, and there is no delete tool to undo it. The empty title is therefore taken from the source — accepted and stored — and the fake has no title rule, because inventing one would have the create slice tested against a refusal upstream never sends.
